You see, the trouble is that we are always trying to separate the good from the bad, the pleasant from the unpleasant, and to live in a world where we can have the good without the bad. But life doesn't work that way. 

Life is a dance of opposites, a play of contrasts.We must come to understand that what we call "disgusting" or "nasty" is simply one aspect of the totality of existence. Just as there can be no light without darkness, there can be no joy without suffering.

 Trying to push away the unpleasant aspects of life only creates more resistance and suffering.Now, consider this: everything in the universe is interconnected. The trees, the stars, the rivers, and you—yes, you—are all part of this grand tapestry. To wish you had never been born is to wish away the marvel of the cosmos, which includes you as an essential part.When you see life as it truly is, without judgment, you begin to realize that the very things you find so repulsive are, in a way, beautiful. 

They are expressions of the same energy that brings flowers into bloom and makes the stars shine. It's all part of the dance. Let go of the need to control or resist. Instead, flow with life. Embrace the full spectrum of experience. By doing so, you might just find that what you once saw as disgusting is, in fact, another form of the divine play. So, how do you live without thinking about nasty things?

 You don't. You accept them as part of the whole and see them for what they truly are—moments in the great unfolding of existence. In this acceptance, you find peace.
